core_obligations: Get the existence of the isomorphism from the Cohen structure theorem, noting the author's footnote that in characteristic p the theorem yields a surjection from a Cohen ring that factors through kappa (proof lines 4060-4067).

Produce the counterexample showing that in general the isomorphism cannot be chosen as a k-algebra isomorphism: over k = F_p(t), the completion of A = k[x,y]/(y^2 + x^p - t) at (y) is k(t^{1/p})[[z]] as a ring, but contains no element whose p-th power is t, visible modulo y^2 (proof lines 4069-4078).

In the separable case, lift kappa to a k-algebra map into the completion, send the variables to generators f_i of the maximal ideal, and deduce surjectivity from adic completeness of both sides plus surjectivity modulo the augmentation ideal (proof lines 4080-4097).
proof_roadmap: Apply the Cohen structure theorem (proof lines 4060-4067).
Show the k-algebra statement can fail by an explicit completion computation (proof lines 4069-4078).
Construct the k-algebra isomorphism in the separable case (proof lines 4080-4097).
difficulty_reason: For a locally Noetherian scheme X over a field k and a point x with residue field kappa, the lemma produces an isomorphism kappa[[x_1, ..., x_n]]/I to the completion of the local ring at x inducing the identity on residue fields, and determines exactly when it can be chosen as a k-algebra isomorphism (statement lines 4043-4057). The first half is an application of the Cohen structure theorem, with the author's own footnote explaining how the mixed characteristic form of the theorem reduces to the displayed one (proof lines 4060-4067). The second half is where the lemma acquires independent content: the author exhibits an explicit example over k = F_p(t), namely A = k[x,y]/(y^2 + x^p - t) completed at the maximal ideal (y), whose completion is isomorphic to k(t^{1/p})[[z]] as a ring but not as a k-algebra, because no element of the completion has p-th power t, as one sees modulo y^2 (proof lines 4069-4078). The positive direction for separable kappa/k is then a separate construction: lift kappa to a k-algebra homomorphism into the completion, send x_i to generators of the maximal ideal, and use that both sides are adically complete and that the map is surjective modulo the ideal, hence surjective (proof lines 4080-4097). The claim is H3: the lemma carries a counterexample construction and a separability criterion of its own, not merle restating the structure theorem.
